title: The secret handshake
kid: Your phone and the video server do a secret handshake before the film starts. The phone checks the server's gold stamp, then both sides mix colours so they get the same lock colour. After that, every parcel travels locked.
nerd: TLS 1.3 starts with SNI and certificate authentication: video.example presents a chain leaf → intermediate → root in the trust store, with a matching name and valid dates. X25519 ECDHE exchanges public shares g^a and g^b; both endpoints derive g^ab with HKDF and protect records with AEAD such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8446, one round trip).

cdn.title: The server proves who it is
cdn.kid: The video server shows its ID card with a gold stamp. It mixes its secret colour too, so it gets the very same lock colour as your phone. Then it sends video parcels that only the two ends can open.
cdn.nerd: At the server endpoint, TLS terminates: the certificate for video.example is sent, the selected TLS 1.3 cipher suite is used, and the server's X25519 secret combines with the client's public share to derive the same traffic keys. Records leave as authenticated ciphertext.

sealed.title: What the crow can see
sealed.kid: This stop carries the parcel, but it cannot open the lock. Like the crow, it sees the orange and green mixtures and then locked parcels with scrambled marks. Even the boxes that carry your parcel cannot read it.
sealed.nerd: At {hop}, TLS is sealed end to end. The hop can forward lower-layer headers, but TLS records are AEAD ciphertext; it may observe SNI/certificate handshake metadata and ECDHE public shares, not the HTTP request or keys.
